description_full: Evolution Mining Limited engages in the exploration, mine development and operation, and sale of gold and gold-copper concentrates in Australia and Canada. It explores for copper and silver deposits. The company was formerly known as Catalpa Resources Limited and changed its name to Evolution Mining Limited in November 2011. Evolution Mining Limited was incorporated in 1998 and is based in Sydney, Australia.

financial_summary: Evolution Mining Ltd. is a large-cap basic materials business with a $18.1B market cap on $3.8B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +36% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +7.4pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 10% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, with gross margins sitting at 49%.
The business throws off $970M in free cash flow — roughly 26 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.0× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 18× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 1.9%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 3.3× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

Trade policy and tariff whiplash — materials producers are first-order casualties of protectionist swings, and margin gets squeezed from both input and output pricing.
